--   - sp_customer_tier: recompute the lifetime tier of every active customer
--     (GOLD >= 1000, SILVER >= 500, otherwise BRONZE) into customer_tiers.
--   - sp_monthly_report: rebuild the per-category revenue report for a given

-- Null handling uses COALESCE, timestamps use now(), and single-row fetches
-- use LIMIT 1 instead of the original row-limiting constructs.
-- ============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_customer_tier()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $proc$
DECLARE
    v_tier   varchar(20);
    v_status varchar(20);
    rec      record;
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM customer_tiers;

    FOR rec IN (
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               c.customer_name,
               SUM(o.order_total) AS total_spend,
               COUNT(*)           AS order_count
        FROM   orders o
        JOIN   customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
        WHERE  COALESCE(c.status, 'ACTIVE') = 'ACTIVE'
        GROUP  BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
        ORDER  BY total_spend, o.customer_id
    ) LOOP
        IF rec.total_spend >= 1000 THEN
            v_tier := 'GOLD';
        ELSIF rec.total_spend >= 500 THEN
            v_tier := 'SILVER';
        ELSE
            v_tier := 'BRONZE';
        END IF;

        INSERT INTO customer_tiers
            (customer_id, customer_name, total_spend, order_count, tier, computed_at)
        VALUES
            (rec.customer_id, rec.customer_name, rec.total_spend, rec.order_count,
             v_tier, now());
    END LOOP;

    SELECT status INTO v_status FROM customers LIMIT 1;

    COMMIT;
END;

But when the CALL is inside a client-issued explicit transaction block (`BEGIN`), the procedure's COMMIT is NOT allowed — "invalid transaction termination". 

Hmm wait, that doesn't match what I remembered... Let me think. Actually the rule in PG: transaction control in procedures is allowed when the procedure "owns" the transaction — the CALL must be the outermost... Actually I recall now: `PreventInTransactionBlock` — COMMIT in a procedure raises "invalid transaction termination" if... hmm, the actual behavior just demonstrated: CALL inside BEGIN block → COMMIT inside proc → ERROR.
